_comment: One or more upstream sources to sync. Each source is cloned by the workflow via `git clone --sparse` into upstream_checkout_root/@<owner>/<repo>/<branch>/<directory_name>/ BEFORE this script runs. Every output file — both the cleaned JSON under local_output_root and its compiled SRS under srs/ — is namespaced the same way: @<owner>/<repo>/<branch>/<directory_name>/... Owner+repo+branch is already globally unique, so this keeps multiple sources from ever colliding, and keeps the srs tree's top-level naming identical to the synced-file tree's.
_sources_note: Add more entries to 'sources' to sync additional repos/directories — e.g. a second entry with owner 'SagerNet', repo 'sing-geosite', branch 'rule-set', upstream_path 'geosite', directory_name 'geosite'. Each source's files land under its own @owner/repo/branch/directory_name namespace in both local_output_root and srs/, so nothing overwrites another source's files even if filenames match. 'directory_name' defaults to the last path segment of upstream_path if omitted.
_custom_note: The custom/ directory (multi-level subdirectories supported) holds your own hand-maintained JSON rule-sets — checked into this repo directly, not fetched from anywhere. Every run, files under custom/ go through the same blacklist cleanup as any other source, get written to rules/custom/<...>.json, and get compiled to srs/custom/<...>.srs (dated + latest), exactly like a configured source. If custom/ doesn't exist or is empty, it's silently skipped.
_cdn_note: cdn_owner/cdn_repo (used only as a fallback if GITHUB_REPOSITORY isn't set) identify the repo HOSTING these files for jsDelivr — i.e. this repo, not any upstream source. cdn_ref_mode 'tag' links dated SRS snapshots and JSON to the exact release tag just created this run; the 'latest' SRS catalog always links against cdn_branch regardless of this setting, since its contents change every run.
